Class MarkdownDetector

java.lang.Object
org.casserole.format.markdown.MarkdownDetector
All Implemented Interfaces:
FormatDetector
public class MarkdownDetector extends Object implements FormatDetector
The MarkdownDetector type matches CommonMark structure in a whole reply. CommonMark is the markdown dialect this detector parses. A heading, a fenced code block, or a block quote is structure. A bullet list or an ordered list is structure only when the reply has at least two list items. A single paragraph does not match, even when that paragraph contains emphasis.

  • Method Details

    • matches

      public boolean matches(String raw)
      The matches method parses the reply and looks for structure. A null reply or a blank reply returns false. A heading, a fenced code block, or a block quote sets the structure flag. List items are counted across every bullet list and ordered list. Two or more list items also set the structure flag. The method returns true only when structure was seen and either the item count is at least two or hasHeadingFenceOrQuote(Node) is true. A list of one item with no heading, fence, or quote returns false.
      Specified by:
      matches in interface FormatDetector
      Parameters:
      raw - The full assistant text.
      Returns:
      true when the reply has a heading, a fence, a quote, or at least two list items.

    • hasHeadingFenceOrQuote

      private boolean hasHeadingFenceOrQuote(org.commonmark.node.Node doc)
      The hasHeadingFenceOrQuote method looks at the top-level children of the document. The method returns true when one child is a heading, a fenced code block, or a block quote. Nested nodes are not visited.
      Parameters:
      doc - The parsed document.
      Returns:
      true when a top-level heading, fence, or quote is present.

    • countItems

      private int countItems(org.commonmark.node.Node list)
      The countItems method counts the direct children that are list items. A child that is not a list item is not counted.
      Parameters:
      list - The bullet list or ordered list node.
      Returns:
      The number of direct list-item children.
